q: Since Java 8, where is class metadata stored?
explain: PermGen was removed in Java 8. Metaspace grows in native memory and is unbounded by default, so set `MaxMetaspaceSize` if class generation could leak.

q: What is the most common cause of `StackOverflowError`?
options: Too many objects on the heap
explain: Each call adds a frame to the thread's stack (size set by `-Xss`). Typical culprits: missing base cases, cyclic `toString`/`equals`, bidirectional JPA entities serialized to JSON.

q: Which of these is NOT a GC root?
options: An object referenced only from another unreachable object
A local variable in an active stack frame
A static field of a loaded class
explain: Being referenced isn't enough: the referencing object must itself be reachable from a root.

q: Objects A and B reference each other, and nothing else references either. What happens at the next full GC?
options: Neither is collected: they keep each other alive
Only the older one is collected
It's a memory leak until the JVM restarts
explain: Java GCs trace reachability from roots. Cycles are a problem only for reference counting, which the JVM doesn't use.

q: What is the generational hypothesis?
options: Old objects reference young ones more often than the reverse
Objects are accessed in creation order
explain: So the young generation is collected often with cheap copying, and only survivors pay for promotion.

q: Which GC is the default since Java 9 (on server-class machines)?
explain: G1 replaced Parallel as the default in JDK 9 (JEP 248). On very small machines (1 CPU or under ~1.8 GB) the JVM still picks Serial.

q: You need sub-millisecond GC pauses on a 100 GB heap. Which collector?
explain: ZGC does marking and relocation concurrently, so pauses don't grow with the heap. G1's pause goal is a target, not a guarantee, and 1 ms is unrealistic for it.

q: In G1, what is a humongous object?
options: An object at least half a region in size, allocated straight into contiguous old regions
Any object larger than 1 MB in Eden
An array of more than a million elements
explain: Humongous allocations skip the young gen and can fragment the heap. Many of them is a sign to increase `G1HeapRegionSize` or avoid huge arrays.

q: When is a SoftReference cleared?
options: Under memory pressure, and always before an OutOfMemoryError
explain: Soft references survive while memory is plentiful, which once made them popular for caches. A real cache with size limits (Caffeine) is more predictable.

q: An object is only reachable through WeakReferences. When is it collected?
options: At the next GC that processes it
When the WeakReference is enqueued manually
explain: Weak references don't keep objects alive at all. That's how WeakHashMap entries disappear.

q: What is the status of `Object.finalize()`?
options: Deprecated for removal; use try-with-resources or Cleaner
The recommended way to release native resources
Called deterministically when an object is unreachable
explain: Finalization is unpredictable, slows GC and can resurrect objects. JEP 421 (JDK 18) deprecated it for removal.

q: What does `OutOfMemoryError: GC overhead limit exceeded` mean?
options: The JVM spends almost all its time in GC while recovering very little memory
Too many GC threads were started
The GC log file is full
explain: With the Parallel GC the threshold is over 98% of time in GC recovering under 2% of the heap. It usually means a leak or a heap that's simply too small.

q: A JVM runs in a container with a 2 GB memory limit and no -Xmx. What's the default max heap?
explain: Modern JVMs are container-aware and default `MaxRAMPercentage` to 25. Services usually set it to 60–75%, leaving room for metaspace, threads and direct memory.

q: What can escape analysis let the JIT do?
options: Replace a non-escaping object with locals, so it's never allocated on the heap
Move objects to the old generation earlier
explain: Scalar replacement splits an object into its fields. It also enables lock elision on objects no other thread can see.

q: Why is object allocation in Java so cheap?
options: Each thread bumps a pointer in its own TLAB, with no synchronization
Objects are allocated on the stack
Allocation is lazy until first use
explain: A TLAB is a chunk of Eden reserved for one thread. Allocation is a pointer increment plus a bounds check; only a new TLAB needs coordination.

q: What is the card table for?
options: Tracking old-to-young references, so a minor GC doesn't scan the whole old generation
Recording which threads are at a safepoint
explain: A write barrier marks the card (a small heap chunk) when a reference field is written. A minor GC scans only dirty cards as extra roots.

q: Which tool shows what retains the most memory in a heap dump?
explain: MAT's dominator tree shows objects whose removal would free the most memory, and "path to GC roots" shows why they're still alive.

q: `OutOfMemoryError: unable to create native thread`. What's the likely cause?
options: The OS thread limit or native memory is exhausted, not the heap
explain: Each platform thread needs an OS thread and native stack memory. Look for thread leaks (pools created per request), or check `ulimit -u` and container pid limits.

q: Why can't an application replace `java.lang.String` with its own class of the same name?
options: Parent delegation: the bootstrap loader always loads it first
The class name is reserved by the compiler
The JVM verifies a signature on every core class
explain: A class loader asks its parent before loading itself, and `java.*` packages are also protected from being defined by user loaders.

q: What does `System.gc()` do?
options: Suggests a GC; the JVM may ignore it
Forces an immediate full GC every time
explain: Usually it triggers a full GC, but it's only a hint and `-XX:+DisableExplicitGC` turns it off. Calling it in application code is almost always wrong.

q: Why do servers often set `-Xms` equal to `-Xmx`?
options: To avoid heap resizing at runtime and claim memory up front
It makes the heap use huge pages
explain: Growing and shrinking the heap costs extra GCs, and a fixed size makes the memory footprint predictable, which matters for containers.

q: What does a stop-the-world pause mean?
options: All application threads are paused at a safepoint while the GC works
Only the allocating thread is paused
The JVM process is suspended by the OS
explain: Even concurrent collectors have short STW phases. A thread in a long loop without safepoint polls can delay everyone (time-to-safepoint).

q: What is the maximum tenuring threshold in HotSpot?
explain: Object age is stored in 4 bits of the header. Objects can be promoted earlier if Survivor space overflows (premature promotion).

q: `NoClassDefFoundError` vs `ClassNotFoundException`?
options: NoClassDefFoundError: class present at compile time but missing or failed to init at runtime; ClassNotFoundException: explicit loading by name failed
ClassNotFoundException is an Error; NoClassDefFoundError is checked
explain: `NoClassDefFoundError` often hides an earlier `ExceptionInInitializerError` in a static initializer. Check the first error in the log.
